guias.title: Porsche 964 guide: versions, common faults and buying advice
guias.metaTitulo: Porsche 964: buying guide, common faults and servicing
guias.metaDescripcion: Porsche 964 guide, built from 1989 to 1994: versions, key inspection points, M64 engine faults and the servicing this generation needs.
guias.excerpt: Which Porsche 964 to choose, what to check before buying it and what symptoms should not be treated as normal in an air-cooled 911 that is already over thirty years old.
entradilla: The Porsche 964 maintains the size and appearance of a classic 911, but introduced a much more modern technical foundation: power steering, ABS, more complex air conditioning, automatic rear spoiler and, in the Carrera 4, all-wheel drive. This combination explains its current appeal, although it also means that an apparently simple car can accumulate electrical, hydraulic and air conditioning faults that do not exist in previous generations.

From a workshop perspective, the key is how the car has been driven and documented, rather than an advertised low mileage. A regularly used 964 with controlled oil leaks, a serviced twin-ignition system and renewed suspension is usually a more sensible purchase than one stored for years and prepared only for sale. The inspection should distinguish tolerable oil misting from an active leak, and genuine preservation from cosmetic restoration.

This guide is for comparing versions and ordering an inspection before purchasing. It is not a substitute for measuring compression and leaks, inspecting the underbody and checking numbers, history and equipment on the specific car. On a 964, a small difference in condition can mean a big difference in budget during the first few years of ownership.

ficha.valor: Air-cooled six-cylinder boxer, 3,6 l; Turbo 3,3 and 3,6 l

versiones.texto: First introduced for the 1989 model year, with 3,6 litres and 250 CV. Its mechanical all-wheel-drive system provides safety, but adds transmission, actuators and maintenance that must be checked methodically.

Since the 1990 model year, with 250 CV, rear propulsion and manual or Tiptronic transmission. It is the most direct base for those looking for regular use and a less complex architecture than that of the Carrera 4.
Lightened version from 1992, with 260 CV in European specification; the later RS 3.8 reached 300 CV. Suspension, brakes, bodywork and authenticity weigh as much as the condition of the engine.

Manufactured since 1990 with 320 CV; the Turbo S reached 381 CV in very limited-production configurations. Retains the power delivery of the 930 family and requires checking turbo, CIS, ignition and temperature.
Launched for 1993 with 360 CV and greater torque. Its value makes it especially important to verify identity, factory equipment, structural repairs and engine and gearbox correspondence.

The 1993 Speedster and editions like the 30 Jahre have limited production and specific details. Before paying the premium, it is advisable to document that these elements do not come from a subsequent transformation.

antesDeComprar: Ask for invoices, not just service-book stamps. Look for dates for adjustments, clutch and dual-mass flywheel, maintenance of the double distributor, shock absorbers, flexible tubes, air conditioning and leak repair. A coherent dossier makes it possible to distinguish credible mileage from an odometer reading without context.

With the engine cold, observe engine cranking, smoke, and timing system noises. Then measure compression and cylinder leaks, examines spark plugs and checks hot oil pressure. The state is not decided by a photograph of the clean block or by a single compression figure.

Check cylinder head and cylinder joints, rocker covers, return pipes, seals and area between engine and gearbox. The first M64 engines without a head gasket deserve special attention, but not all of them need to be opened: real loss, gases, oil consumption and evolution must be assessed.

Check that both rotors receive spark and that the distributor has proper ventilation. A broken internal belt can leave the engine running on a single ignition, raise temperatures and cause detonation without the driver immediately realizing the cause.

Measure paint thicknesses and examine turrets, wings, cross members, window frames, rain gutters, floors and lifting points. Corrosion is usually hidden under rubber or old repairs. Irregular alignments can indicate a poorly resolved shot.

Test the heating, air conditioning, fans, automatic spoiler, roof and electric windows. On the Carrera 4, check the differential locks, warning lights and absence of judder. On Tiptronic models, check that every gear engages smoothly and that the oil does not smell burnt.

averias.texto: A light oil film does not equal a puddle after each stop. The smell of burnt oil, smoke from the exchangers, fresh drops or dirt that reappears after cleaning requires the source to be located. Ignoring it deteriorates hoses, fouls the cooling and can turn an exterior repair into a major intervention.

The engine can continue to start when one of the two banks of spark plugs has stopped firing. Strange idling, unresponsiveness, or an uneven spark check warrant stopping the diagnosis. Maintaining ventilation and checking the belt avoids working with inadequate temperatures and combustion.

averias.titulo: Dual-mass flywheel, clutch and G50 gearbox
averias.texto: Vibration at idle, rattling when shutting off, uneven pedal, slipping clutch or scratching gears point to different wear. The test must be done with the engine cold and hot; Continuing to drive can damage synchronizers, support and transmission, in addition to making clutch replacement more expensive.

Original shock absorbers, hardened rubber bushes and loose ball joints make a 964 seem nervous or imprecise. It is not corrected with an alignment if the clearances are not first eliminated. An update restores stability and prevents abnormal tyre wear.

Different temperatures between outlets, fans that only work at one speed, a battery that discharges or a spoiler that does not complete its journey require electrical diagnosis. Changing parts by trial and error is usually expensive and does not resolve damaged connectors, relays, sensors or control units.

Bubbles under the rubber, humidity in the trunk or thick filler are rarely an isolated defect. You must open the inspection area and assess the extent of the corrosion before budgeting for paint. Covering it without removing the corrosion compromises structure and value.

mantenimiento: Have an annual inspection even if the car only travels a few kilometres. Oil and filter, leaks, pressure, belts, ignition, brakes, tyres, lights and levels offer a repeatable snapshot of the condition. In cars with sporadic use, time ages fuel, tyres, brake fluid and connections even if the odometer does not advance.

Alternate basic and major maintenance service depending on history and usage. The major should include spark plugs, filters, valve adjustment when applicable, inspection of the double distributor, belts, fuel lines, transmission and planned retightening. The rate guides the scope; the final budget depends on the findings.

Renew brake fluid for time and monitor flexes, calipers and discs. In Carrera 4 it adds fluids and integral transmission checks. At Tiptronic, don't treat oil as permanent: check level, colour, leaks and documented service to the correct specification.

If the car spends weeks stopped, maintain the battery with appropriate equipment, fill it with fresh fuel and avoid starting it for just a few minutes. It is preferable to complete a route that brings oil and exhaust to temperature and allows the brakes, bearings, air conditioning and spoiler to be moved.
loQueHemosHecho: At Valentín Motors we have documented the restoration of M64 engines, including measurement, machining, assembly and post-testing, as well as complete projects on the 964 Turbo.
These works show why prior diagnosis matters: two cars with the same symptom can require anything from a peripheral repair to a rebuild, and the budget should not be decided before measuring.
aQuienLeConviene: It is suitable for those who want a classic 911 that can cope with touring and modern traffic, accept specialist maintenance and value a verifiable history more than a specific colour combination. A manual Carrera 2 is the most direct option; a Carrera 4 provides traction in exchange for complexity; Turbo and RS demand another scale of budget and authentication.

It is not suitable for those looking for the costs of an economical car, long periods of non-use or a purchase based solely on appreciation. If you prefer lighter driving sensations and earlier mechanicals, look at a 911 F or G; if you need easier climate control and daily use, a well-serviced 993 or 996 may be a better fit.

guias.title: Porsche 996 guide: versions, IMS and buying advice
guias.metaTitulo: Porsche 996: buying guide, IMS and common faults
guias.metaDescripcion: Porsche 996 guide, 1997 to 2005: Carrera and Turbo differences, IMS checks, bore scoring and the servicing to assess before buying.
guias.excerpt: How to buy a Porsche 996 without reducing the entire decision to IMS: engines, versions, signs of bore scoring, cooling, chassis and history.
entradilla: The Porsche 996 was the first mass-produced 911 with a water-cooled engine. It shares an industrial approach with the first Boxster, but retains a rear engine, rear seats and a range that goes from the 300 CV Carrera to Turbo, GT3 and GT2. Today it offers usable performance and a compact dimensions, although its purchase price can hide deferred maintenance.

In the workshop it is advisable to divide the family in two. Carrera, Carrera 4 and Targa use M96 engines subject to specific discussion on IMS, bore scoring and cooling system. Turbo, GT2 and GT3 use another architecture derived from the competition engine, known as Mezger; they don't share the same sealed IMS bearing, but they do have expensive needs of their own. Saying that all 996 models suffer from the same thing leads to poorly planned purchases and repairs.

A good unit is not defined by having an advertised solution, but by the whole: operating data, analysed oil, cylinders inspected when appropriate, clean cooling, clearance-free suspension and consistent invoices. The pre-purchase must identify the specific risk and give it context, not promise zero risk.

ficha.valor: Water-cooled six-cylinder boxer, 3,4-3,6 l; Turbo 3,6 l

versiones.texto: The first series, from 1997 to 2001, delivered 300 CV and was offered with propulsion or all-wheel drive. Its age is not enough to identify the type of IMS: the engine and actual configuration must be checked.
The 996.2 update, from 2001, rose to 320 CV and adopted the Turbo front. Includes Carrera 2, Carrera 4, Cabriolet and Targa, with differences in weight and complexity.

It combines a wide body, brakes and appearance close to the Turbo with a 320 CV naturally aspirated engine. Its attractiveness does not eliminate the risks of the M96 and adds more transmission elements and higher-cost tyres.

The Turbo develops 420 CV, or 450 CV with the X50 and in the final Turbo S. Its engine does not use the Carrera's sealed IMS; Coolant pipes, turbos, clutch, spoiler and integral transmission must be checked.

360 CV in the first series and 381 CV in the second, with a Mezger engine, manual transmission and focused chassis. It is essential to read hours and over-rev events ranges and check if the track use had the corresponding maintenance.
Rear propulsion, twin-turbo engine and 462 CV, up to 483 CV in the final evolution. Authenticity, structural condition, and usage history outweigh a cursory visual inspection.

antesDeComprar: Identify version, model year, engine and gearbox code using VIN and tags, and match them with invoices. Do not infer the IMS bearing by the registration date: a motor may have been replaced, opened or exchanged, and the only useful data is the present and documented configuration.

On naturally aspirated Carrera models, combine diagnostic readings, oil-filter inspection, oil analysis and borescope inspection when there is oil consumption, smoke, noise or suspicion of bore scoring. Inspect every cylinder consistently and assess the marks alongside compression, leak-down results and engine behaviour.

Check cold starting, pressure, rattles, smoke and idle stabilization. When hot, observe oil pressure, temperature and smoke after overrun. Mixture of oil and coolant, metal particles or a knock that changes with load warrant stopping operation until diagnosed.

Check radiators and condensers behind the bumpers, water pump, expansion tank, cap and coolant remains. Accumulated leaves promote corrosion and loss of efficiency; a loose pump can release material and cause overheating.

Read operating hours and rev ranges on manual cars, and check that mileage, interior wear and history are consistent. In Turbo and GT it also checks stuck or fixed pipes, turbos, intercoolers, clutch and possible power preparations.

Test suspension on uneven ground, brakes from speed, air conditioning, windows, closures, roof and spoiler. Aging arms, engine mounts, shock absorbers and cups alter stability; Tiptronic requires clean changes, without delays or bumps.

averias.texto: Particles in the filter, leaks in the shaft area, abnormal synchronization or noise should not wait for the next inspection. The risk and solution depend on the bearing fitted, the condition of the engine and whether the gearbox is to be removed. Replacing one part without inspecting the rest does not make the engine new.

Increased oil consumption, smoke from one cylinder bank, uneven soot in exhausts and hot knocking can accompany cylinder scoring. Borescope inspection confirms and localizes, but its interpretation must be combined with measurements. Continuing to use the car worsens piston and cylinder-liner damage and contaminates the oil.

A drop between the engine and gearbox may come from the rear seal, but intense smoke after idling, whistling and excessive vacuum lead to the oil separator. Changing the RMS reflexively without locating the source may require dismounting twice. A failing AOS also contaminates intake and catalytic converters.

Unstable temperature, sweet smell, frequent fans or pink residue require pressure testing. Impeller, thermostat, expansion tank, hoses and radiators work as a system; Ignoring a small leak can end in overtemperature and deformation of cylinder heads.

Sharp knocks, floating steering, inner wear of the tyre or engine movements when accelerating indicate different clearances. Before aligning, check arms, linkages, cups, shock absorbers, supports and bearings. A healthy chassis also helps detect a poorly repaired body.

averias.titulo: Turbo and GT pipework and ancillary components
averias.texto: In Mezger engines, coolant unions, oil tubes, actuators, turbos and clutch must be inspected. Loss under load, coolant smell or smoke are not normal features of a powerful version; a leak in heavy use can empty the circuit quickly.

mantenimiento: An annual oil and filter inspection allows you to open the filter, control particles and establish a consumption and leak trend. Mileage alone does not protect a stopped car: brake fluid, coolant, belts, tyres, gaskets and fuel also age.

The complete maintenance service should include spark plugs, filters, auxiliary belts, coils, underbody, brakes and cooling circuit. Adjust the interval for urban use, circuit or short trips. If history is lacking, create a baseline before investing in cosmetic improvements.

In Tiptronic, manual gearbox and differentials, check lubricant level, leaks and date. In Turbo and GT it adds boost pressure, intake sealing and pipe fixing. An oil change won't fix worn synchronizers or a faulty converter, but it helps discover the problem early.

Periodically clean radiators and drains without damaging fins, and check the space between radiator and condenser. Maintain homogeneous tyre pressures and age per axle. After intervening suspension, perform geometry with correct heights and loads.
loQueHemosHecho: We have documented the breakage of the intermediate shaft on an M96 3.4 and the subsequent rebuild process. The case allows us to see damages, measurements and decisions that a generic description of the IMS does not show.
We also inspect cooling, bore scoring and transmission before recommending an intervention. The priority is to know if the engine is healthy, locally repairable, or in need of rebuilding.
aQuienLeConviene: It is suitable for those who want to get into a modern 911 of reasonable size, will use it and reserve budget for a diagnostic-based maintenance update. A simple manual Carrera offers the essential experience; a 4S prioritises looks and traction; a Turbo is another architecture and another scale of consumables.

It is not suitable for those who expect that installing an IMS will eliminate all risk or buy the cheapest unit without inspection. If you're looking for air-cooled character, the 964 or 993 are more expensive alternatives; if you prefer a more modern interior and round headlights, compare with a 997, without forgetting that it also requires a specific engine inspection.

guias.title: Porsche 997 guide: versions, common faults and buying advice
guias.metaTitulo: Porsche 997: buying guide, bore scoring and servicing
guias.metaDescripcion: Porsche 997 guide, 2004 to 2012: how 997.1 and 997.2 differ, bore scoring, IMS, PDK and the key checks for a pre-purchase inspection.
guias.excerpt: The differences that change a Porsche 997 purchase: M96/M97 and MA1 engines, Carrera versus Turbo/GT, diagnosis and deferred costs.
entradilla: The Porsche 997 restored round headlights and refined the 996 platform, but the range covers different mechanical specifications. The first series uses M96/M97 engines in the Carrera and the Mezger architecture in Turbo and GT models; the 997.2 update introduces direct injection, MA1 engines and PDK in the regular road models. That distinction matters more in the workshop than a bumper change.

A well-kept car is still fast, compact and easy to use. It can also cause a substantial repair bill if oil consumption has been treated as normal, gearbox service has been omitted, or it has been prepared for track use without documenting it. The inspection must assess the car as a complete system: engine, cooling, transmission, brakes, suspension, body and operating data.

The goal of the guide is to decide which version is best for your use and what to measure before negotiating a purchase. IMS and bore scoring deserve attention, but they do not replace checking for knocks, localized corrosion, radiators, clutch, PDK, PASM or the specific Turbo and GT elements.

ficha.valor: Six-cylinder boxer, 3,6-4,0 l; naturally aspirated or twin-turbo
Manual, Tiptronic in 997.1 or PDK in 997.2

versiones.texto: Since 2004, with 3,6 litres and 325 CV; the Carrera S uses 3,8 litres and 355 CV. The 3,8 deserves a particularly careful check of cylinders and oil consumption.
Since 2008, direct injection engines with 345 CV in Carrera and 385 CV in Carrera S. The sealed IMS of the previous design disappears and PDK and revised electronics arrive.
They add all-wheel drive; Targa features a glass roof and tailgate. Purchase must include equivalent tyres, silent transmission, and full functioning roof, drains, and sunshade.
The 997.1 Turbo offers 480 CV with a Mezger engine; the 997.2 goes to direct injection and 500 CV, with Turbo S of 530 CV. Pipes, turbo geometry, brakes and transmission require their own budget.
From 415 CV in the GT3 3.6 to 450 CV in the RS 4.0. Hours, over revs, track usage, brakes, cage and specific parts must match the history and factory settings.
Rear propulsion and twin-turbo engine, with 530 CV in GT2 and 620 CV in GT2 RS. In these units authentication and a professional structural measurement are not optional.

antesDeComprar: Please confirm whether it is 997.1 or 997.2 by model year, VIN and engine code, not exterior parts. A car can have updated rear lights or PCM without having changed its architecture. Also check relevant options like PASM, differential, ceramic brakes, Sport Chrono and seats.

In Carrera 997.1, he inspects the filter and oil, records consumption and performs a borescope if the history, symptoms or the engine advise it. Marked soot on an exhaust, hot knocking and one-sided smoke raise the suspicion of bore scoring, especially on the 3.8.

Establish which IMS bearing is fitted to the early engines, but do not base a purchase solely on an invoice for its replacement. Check the part used, who installed it and what was inspected. Many later 997.1 models have a larger-diameter bearing that cannot be removed in the same way without opening the engine.

Read over-rev events hours and ranges, stored faults, ignition counters and adaptations. Relate them to mileage, clutch and wear. A recent high-ranking event, or data deleted without explanation, warrants further testing before deciding.

Check the front underneath, radiators, condensers, pump, thermostat and coolant traces. In Turbo/GT it examines cooling and oil pipe joints, supercharging, exhausts and any increase in power. A reprogram changes the thermal load and history reading.

Try PDK or Tiptronic with the engine cold and warm, slow maneuvers and moderate full load. On manual models, look at the clutch, synchronizers and flywheel. Evaluates PASM, dynamic mounts, front-axle lift, PCCB and centre-lock wheels with appropriate tools and procedures.

averias.texto: Scratches are not diagnosed by reputation nor are they ruled out because the car runs well. Oil consumption, hot ticking noise, uneven soot and marks seen from the correct angle make up the set of symptoms. If it progresses, it increases slack, pollution and the cost of reconstruction.

The first Carrera retain IMS bearings and may have leaks from RMS or other nearby joints. Each configuration requires a different procedure. A stain between the engine and gearbox must be cleaned and located before attributing it to the seal or deciding to dismantle it.

Frequently active fans, fluctuating temperature, sweet smell or dry residue require pressure testing and cleaning the front cooling pack. A circuit that loses thermal capacity increases the risk to the engine, gearbox and air conditioning, although the indicator still does not signal an alarm.

Knocking when selecting, shaking clutches, skipping gear or slow synchronization are different symptoms. The diagnosis should include wear and temperature values when available. Driving until the gearbox goes into emergency limits repair options.

Wet shock absorber, PASM warning, bouncing or imprecise support changes indicate that one geometry is not enough. Arms, bushings, engine mounts and tyres are evaluated together. On dynamic engine mounts, the fault may be registered before it is evident when driving.

averias.titulo: Turbo and GT: pipework and hard use
averias.texto: Coolant joint leaks, fatigued actuators, exhaust cracks or overheated brakes have quick consequences under load. Also check the underside of the body, support points and over-rev. A well-maintained track car may be better than a road car with a sketchy history, but it has to be proven.

mantenimiento: Maintain an annual inspection with oil and filter, even below the official mileage, if short or seasonal use predominates. Opening the filter and recording consumption provides historical information. Do not change viscosity to hide noise or consumption without diagnosing the cause.

Complete service includes spark plugs, filters, belt, coils, cooling, brakes and underbody. In direct injection engines, add attention to injectors, fuel pressure and intake deposits when there are failures or loss of performance.

Respect scheduled servicing of PDK, Tiptronic, differentials and all-wheel drive system. Check the clutch and linkage on manual models. After renewing suspension or tyres, adjust geometry according to version and use, not with a generic value for all 997 models.

Clean the radiator-condenser package, renew brake fluid and check tyre age. At PCCB, you measure status with the proper method and avoid judging by appearance alone. For the circuit, it reduces intervals and records temperatures, pads and tightening torques.
loQueHemosHecho: Documented in the Magazine is an M97 engine taken from 3,8 to 4,0 litres with specific cylinder solutions, a rehabilitation of the 997.1 Turbo and the installation of a nose lift on a 997.1.
There are three examples of different needs: correcting an internal fault, rebuilding a supercharged mechanics and adapting the use without compromising the whole.
aQuienLeConviene: It suits anyone who wants a compact-feeling 911 with modern equipment and is willing to choose by engine and history. A 997.2 Carrera reduces some of the concerns associated with the 997.1, but cooling, injection, PDK and chassis systems still need attention. The 997.1 can be an excellent purchase if its measurements are sound and the price reflects its maintenance needs.

It is not suitable for those who only accept binary answers about IMS or bore scoring. If you're looking for a lower cost of entry, compare an inspected 996; if you prioritise more modern cabin and assistance, a 991. Turbo and GT are not simply faster Carrera models: they require appropriate consumables, diagnosis and budget.

guias.title: Porsche 993 guide: versions, common faults and buying advice
guias.metaTitulo: Porsche 993: buying guide, common faults and servicing
guias.metaDescripcion: Porsche 993 guide, 1994 to 1998: Carrera, Turbo and RS, rust-prone areas, oil leaks, ignition, suspension and pre-purchase checks.
guias.excerpt: What to check on the last air-cooled 911: body, engine, Varioram, dual ignition, multi-link chassis and real history.
entradilla: The Porsche 993 is the last air-cooled production 911 and the first with a multi-link rear axle that clearly changed its behaviour. It retains compact dimensions, but its bodywork, air conditioning, electronics and suspension are more complex than in a 964. This mix explains why a car with shiny paint may require a significant investment beneath rubber seals, covers and wheel arches.

The buying decision depends less by the reputation of robustness than by the execution of maintenance. Leaks, valve guides, dual ignition, dual-mass flywheel, evaporator and rubber bushes age in different ways. On high value cars, options, colour, numbers and structural repairs must also be authenticated before discussing whether a mileage is low.

The pre-purchase inspection must begin cold, continue on the lift and end with diagnosis and road testing. A 993 can tolerate small traces of use; it is not advisable to treat as normal persistent smoke, rust in the structure, loose steering or disabled air conditioning because its repair is laborious.

versiones.texto: 3,6 litres, 272 CV at the start and 285 CV with Varioram from 1995/1996 depending on market and model year. Rear propulsion, manual or Tiptronic transmission and narrow body.
Lighter and simpler all-wheel drive than the 964 Carrera 4, with the same naturally aspirated power. Check bellows, front transmission, equivalent tyres and absence of tension or noise.

Turbo look wide body. The 4S incorporates all-wheel drive and equipment close to the Turbo; the Carrera S maintains propulsion. The premium requires verification that it is not an aesthetic conversion.
It uses a dedicated sliding glass roof, not the classic removable panel. Its operation, guides, curtain, sealing and parts availability deserve a full test.
Since 1995, twin-turbo, all-wheel drive and 408 CV; the Turbo S reached 450 CV. Check turbos, leaks, transmission, brakes, ducts and authenticity of any preparation.
The RS 3.8 delivers 300 CV; the GT2 starts at 430 CV and evolves to 450 CV. They are rare cars where sports history, bodywork, light parts and numbers require specialist expertise.

antesDeComprar: Check VIN, option tags, colour of origin, and engine and gearbox numbers when value depends on authenticity. Look for job invoices, mileage readings and previous photos. A sealed book without detail does not prove which gaskets, guides, clutch or suspension have been renewed.

Completely cold start and see smoke, tappets, idle and pressure. When hot, test overrun and acceleration, measure leaks and compression if there are doubts and check documented consumption. Smoke after a long overrun can lead to valve guides, but external oil, seals and internal wear must be separated.

Inspect engine valve timing system covers, rocker covers, returns and engine-gearbox connection. Check the double distributor, its belt and ventilation. Checking the spark in the twelve spark plugs and the condition of the cables prevents accepting an engine that is partially working as normal.

Carefully lift windscreen and rear window rubber, check frames, rain gutters, wing bases, rear wheel arches, bumper supports, floors and lifting points. On doors, check the door check-strap mounting: a poorly repaired crack in the pillar reopens.

Test air conditioning for sufficient time. The evaporator can leak without leaving an obvious puddle and replacing it takes many hours. Also check fans, heating, spoiler, windows, lock, roof and parasitic battery consumption.

On the road, look for stability when braking, centred steering and progressive supports. Dry knocks or drift indicate arms, ball joints, shock absorbers or geometry; Old tyres can disguise or amplify the problem. Tiptronic requires smooth operation with the engine cold and hot.

averias.texto: Odor in heating, smoke when stopping or drops on exchangers require locating the leak. Covers and seals can be repaired without opening the engine, while other losses are consistent with internal wear. Cleaning, applying tracer if necessary and checking afterwards avoids estimates based on old dirt.

Blueish smoke during overrun or when accelerating again, increasing consumption and deposits on the spark plugs justify measurements. Allowing wear to progress increases consumption, fouls chambers and catalytic converters and may end up requiring a more extensive cylinder head inspection.

A faulty internal belt or cable can take part of the dual ignition out of service. The engine still runs, but combustion and temperature worsen. Proper ventilation and periodic inspection are more economical than repairing detonation damage.

averias.titulo: Rust around frames and mounting points
averias.texto: Bubbles next to windows, humidity, recent sealant or weakened bumper supports require partial disassembly before evaluating. Overpainting retains corrosion and can hide a structural repair. The invoice depends on the actual extent, not the visible size.

Hardened rubber bushes, ball joints and worn shock absorbers reduce the precision that distinguishes the 993. If the car ruts, hits or wears tyres unevenly, correct clearances before aligning. Mixing new and spent components produces an inconsistent result.

Recharging the air conditioning every season does not repair a leak. Dropping pressure, odour, irregular fans or lack of heat must be diagnosed by circuit. Postponing the evaporator does not usually break the motor, but it affects use, defrosting and value, and should be included in the purchase price.

mantenimiento: Program oil and filter at least once a year for occasional use and record pressure, leaks and consumption. A repeated visual check allows you to know if sweating remains stable. Check fuel and oil lines, belts and ignition elements for age.

The complete maintenance service includes spark plugs, filters, valve adjustment when applicable, double distributor and leak analysis. Varioram must operate without losses or failures. Do not attribute a lack of power to age until checking ignition, intake and compression.

Renew brake fluid for time and check calipers, discs, hoses and handbrake. Gearboxes and differentials need correct lubricant and leak control; in Carrera 4, it adds front transmission. In Tiptronic it documents service, temperature and fluid status.

The suspension is maintained as a whole: arms, shock absorbers, mounts, ball joints, heights and geometry. After any intervention, fit tyres of a consistent age and specification. A battery maintainer helps, but is not a substitute for regular drives long enough to reach operating temperature.
loQueHemosHecho: The engine and body works published by Valentín Motors on air-cooled generations teach the same method applicable to the 993: disassemble only after diagnosing, measuring before ordering parts and documenting each phase.
When a specific model article does not exist, we avoid presenting another project as if it were. The inspection of the 993 is based on its own architecture and the condition of the specific car.
aQuienLeConviene: It suits those who want the last air-cooled 911 with a more stable chassis and reasonable ergonomics for touring. Carrera and Carrera 4 are usable; S, 4S and Turbo add value, width, consumables and need to authenticate. Condition and traceability justify the premium more than a low odometer reading.

It is not suitable for those who avoid hidden body work or intend to maintain it without a specialist. A 964 offers earlier experience and more classic steering; a 996 costs less and has better air conditioning, but uses water cooling and needs a different inspection checklist.

guias.title: Porsche 930 Turbo guide: versions, common faults and buying advice
guias.metaTitulo: Porsche 930 Turbo: buying guide and common faults
guias.metaDescripcion: Porsche 930 Turbo guide, 1975 to 1989: 3.0 and 3.3, CIS, turbochargers, leaks, corrosion and the essential checks before buying.
guias.excerpt: What to look for in a Porsche 930 before buying: identity, body, fuel, turbo, engine, four-speed gearbox and the unique 1989 G50.
entradilla: The Porsche 930 turned the 911 Turbo into a production model and retained very particular mechanics for years: pronounced turbo lag, air-cooled engine, CIS injection and, until 1988, a four-speed gearbox. It's not a Carrera with wide wings. The thermal load, fuel lines, turbocharger and torque delivery force you to check and drive differently.

Its current value has favored excellent restorations and also reconstructions made to appear correct in photographs. The purchase requires authenticating chassis, engine, gearbox, colour, equipment and original market, measuring the body and documenting any specification changes. A visually transformed 911 G does not thereby acquire the identity of a 930.

From a workshop perspective, the priority is safety before power: fuel and oil system sealing, ignition, mixture, control pressure, brakes, tyres and structure. Only then does it make sense to evaluate boost pressure or improvements. A poor CIS adjustment can cause a car to start and still run dangerously under load.

ficha.valor: Coupe; Targa, Cabriolet and Slantnose in later years

versiones.texto: From 1975 to 1977, with 260 CV in Europe, rear spoiler and specific initial brakes. Its low production makes authenticity and respect for period components essential.
Since 1978, 300 CV, intercooler and redesigned spoiler. It evolves over more than a decade, so brakes, air conditioning, wheels and details must be compared to the exact year.
Some markets received different powers and anti-pollution systems. Import, compression ratio, exhaust and CIS must be identified before comparing figures or ordering parts.
The open bodies arrived in the final stage. Check reinforcements, door fit, soft top, drains and corrosion; Poor structural behaviour is not resolved with new shock absorbers.
Factory Flachbau variants are rare and widely copied. Headlights, wings, intakes, option codes and source documentation should be verified by someone familiar with these series.
Last year, five-speed gearbox and hydraulic clutch. The market premium requires confirmation that the set is original; the driving changes, but does not eliminate engine and bodywork revisions.

antesDeComprar: Start with identity. VIN contrast, engine number, gearbox, paint plate, options and import documentation. Check that spoilers, wings, brakes, interior and wheels correspond to the year. Photograph stamps and look for signs of re-engraving or undocumented substitution.

Measure thickness and geometry, inspect front panel, battery housing, turrets, wheel arches, side sills, pillar base, rear tray and lifting points. An old blow may have displaced anchors even though the outside clearances appear uniform.

Examine fuel lines from the tank to the engine, accumulator, pump, CIS connections and injectors. Odor, humidity or undated hoses prevent a demanding test. In a hot and supercharged space, a small leak has disproportionate consequences.

Start cold and repeat hot. Measure fuel and control pressures, mixture under load, compression and leaks. Observe smoke before and after deceleration with closed throttle, oil pressure and turbo return. Do not adjust mixture to hide a pressure, vacuum or ignition problem.

Check turbo for clearance, leaks, response and pressure, as well as intercooler, wastegate, exhaust and modifications. A car that delivers a high peak power is not necessarily healthy; it can run lean, suffer detonation or exceed the expected pressure.

Test gearbox and clutch that are already warm. In four gears, use synchronizers without forcing; in G50, pedal, cylinders and selection. Check brakes, hoses, bearings, shock absorbers and tyre age before exploring features.

averias.texto: Odor, difficult starting, moisture in fittings or cracked hoses require immobilization and pressure testing. The consequence is not only loss of performance: the fuel can reach ignition, exhaust or turbo. Replace lines with correct material and routing, not a makeshift solution.

averias.titulo: CIS adjustment and incorrect fuel pressure
averias.texto: Prolonged hot starts, fluctuating idle, jerks and lack of fuel under load can come from the accumulator, regulator, air intakes, pumps or injectors. Turning the mixture screw without measuring can hide the symptom at idle and worsen safety at full load.

Persistent blue smoke, oil in intake or exhaust and abnormal response require checking turbo, return, crankcase pressure and engine condition. Changing the turbocharger without correcting the drainage or the cause of overpressure can repeat the fault.

averias.titulo: Studs, cylinder heads and oil leaks
averias.texto: Knocking, cylinder base leak, loss of compression or broken studs call for a complete evaluation. Continuing to increase turbo pressure accelerates the damage. If it is opened, the crankcase, cylinders, cylinder heads, engine valve timing system and lubrication must be measured before defining the scope.

Grinding when downshifting, a gear that doesn't stay in gear, or a clutch that slips under boost are not part of the 930's character. Forcing changes damages teeth and selectors. An early diagnosis separates adjustment, clutch, linkage and gearbox rebuild.

The width of the wings and the value of the model make repairs and conversions frequent. Welds, sealant, point symmetry and thicknesses tell the story. New paint without documentation should prompt more inspection, not more trust.

mantenimiento: Check oil and filter at least every year and control consumption, pressure and temperature under comparable conditions. Inspect screens or plugs when applicable, ducts to the radiator, turbo return and exhaust leaks. Allow temperatures to stabilize before applying load and allow the temperature to drop after intense use.

The complete maintenance service should cover valve timing, spark plugs, ignition, filters, CIS pressures, injectors, belts, turbo and exhaust. Modern fuel and long periods of standstill justify monitoring tanks, pumps and accumulator more frequently.

Renew brake fluid for time and check calipers, discs, flexible tubes and bearings. The power does not compensate for old tyres or exhausted shocks. Adjust geometry and heights after eliminating clearances, respecting the specification and use.

Gearbox, differential and clutch need inspection for leaks and correct lubricant. In 1989 it added a hydraulic clutch. If there is power preparation, reduce intervals and document mixture, pressure, temperature and components; an undocumented modification complicates both diagnosis and resale.
loQueHemosHecho: Valentín Motors has published restorations of 930 Turbo 3.0 and 3.3 engines, a complete restoration of 930 and the recovery of a unit affected by fire.
These cases illustrate two priorities of this guide: check fuel and heat before looking for performance, and measure the body until the real limit of the damage is found.
aQuienLeConviene: It suits a driver who understands the delivery of a classic turbo, will warm up the mechanics, maintain brakes and tyres at the highest level and accepts a technical inspection before pursuing aesthetic originality. The 3.3 offers more availability; a 3.0 or Flachbau requires a more rigorous specialist assessment.

It is not suitable as a first classic if you are looking for progressive reactions, predictable costs or frequent urban use. A naturally aspirated 911 G is more linear; a 964 Turbo adds aids and five gears, although it remains specialist; a 996 Turbo offers much more ease of use with a different architecture.

guias.title: Porsche 356 guide: versions, rust and buying advice
guias.metaTitulo: Porsche 356: buying guide, rust and servicing
guias.metaDescripcion: Porsche 356 guide, 1948 to 1965: Pre-A, A, B and C, authenticity, structural corrosion, engine, brakes and a pre-purchase inspection.
guias.excerpt: Buying a Porsche 356 starts with the structure: how to check for rust, numbers, engine, gearbox, brakes and quality of an old restoration.
entradilla: The Porsche 356 seems mechanically simple, but buying one requires more discipline than buying a modern classic. Its monocoque body depends on side members, floors, cross members and suspension points that may have suffered corrosion and various restorations. An engine that starts well does not compensate for a structure repaired without correct alignment.

The name covers Pre-A, A, B and C, as well as coupé, Cabriolet, Speedster, Roadster and the rare four-cam Carrera versions. During production they changed brakes, gearboxes, engines, windscreens and hundreds of details. Authenticity should be judged against a specific chassis and date, not a generic image of a 356.

From a workshop perspective, the best buy is a unit that allows you to see what was done: photographs of the bare metal, measurements, invoices, numbers and parts removed. An aged but honest restoration may be preferable to fresh paint over unknown welds. This guide sets out the inspection sequence, but a valuable car needs a lift and a specialist.

ficha.valor: Coupe, Cabriolet, Speedster, Convertible D and Roadster

versiones.texto: From 1948 to 1955, with split or curved windscreen depending on the stage and low displacement engines. Scarcity and craft variations make it essential to confirm numbers and details with expert documentation.
From 1955 to 1959, already with T1 and T2 bodywork, 1300 and 1600 engines and various powers. Includes Speedster and Convertible D, highly reproduced and transformed.
From 1959 to 1963, T5 and T6 bodies with visible changes in bumpers, hoods and windows. It offers Normal, Super and Super 90, as well as Roadster and Carrera.
From 1963 to 1965, it incorporated disc brakes on all four wheels and 75 CV 1600 C or 95 CV SC engines. It is usually the easiest to integrate into current traffic.
Light open bodies with great value premium. Check frame, reinforcements, windscreen, seats, soft top and documentation to rule out a coupé conversion or replica.
Four-shaft Fuhrmann engines, from 1,5 to 2,0 litres and much higher powers. Its complexity, pieces and value require a specific specialist; it should not be budgeted as a 1600 rod.

antesDeComprar: Authenticate chassis, identification plate, engine and gearbox numbers, and compare them with available certificates and registrations. Distinguish matching numbers, period-correct engine and simply functional engine. In Speedster, Carrera and early series, a documentary difference substantially changes the value.

Inspect with lift and meter: battery tray, front, side members, floors, cross members, thresholds, pillar bases, wheel arches, front axle support and rear anchors. Look for laps, beads, new sheet metal without interior primer, and closed drains.

Measure diagonals and observe door clearances with the car supported and raised. A door that changes adjustment when lifting reveals flexing. Check wheel camber, axle position and symmetry; a beautiful body can be out of geometry due to corrosion or accident.

Cold start, checks pressure, smoke and noise, and measures compression, leaks and axial play. Examine leaks in the pulley, tubes, covers and crankcase joint. Check carburettors, linkages, heaters and ignition advance without compensating for wear with excessive mixture.

Try all four gears and reductions. Scratching can come from synchronizers, clutch or adjustment, but should not be accepted as normal. Check axle tubes, supports and leaks. Please confirm that the ratio and casing correspond to the version if originality matters.

With drum brakes, check for pulling, out-of-round drums and correct adjustment; on the C, check for leaks and inspect the calipers. Test the 6-volt system, charging, starting, lights and earth connections. Correctly sized tyres and sound dampers matter more than fitting a mismatched selection of modern components.

averias.texto: Rust on floors rarely ends up in the visible area. If it affects side members, front support or pillar bases, rigidity and geometry change. Before estimating, remove sealant at representative points and measure. Replacing panels without a base or references can leave a shiny car that does not drive straight.

averias.titulo: Crankshaft end float and engine wear
averias.texto: Slipping pulley, hot low pressure, smoke and excessive crankcase ventilation require measuring before adjusting. Continuing may damage the crankcase, crankshaft and bearings. A correct rebuild includes dimensions, balancing and evaluation of cylinder heads, not just segments and gaskets.

Loss of compression, blowing, changing settings or uneven spark plugs can indicate seat, guide, crack or fixation. Frequent adjustment will not correct a sagging valve. Diagnosing early prevents a loose part from damaging the piston and chamber.

Difficult starting, backfiring, black spark plugs or high temperature can come from timing, floats, jets, air intakes or advance. Adjusting carburettors on a worn ignition or engine produces temporary results and high consumption.

Scraping in second gear, imprecise lever or noise during overrun must separate the bushings, clutch, supports and synchronizers. Forcing a cold gearbox accelerates wear. The right oil and a tight linkage help, but they don't rebuild worn surfaces.

A poorly centred drum or a wet cylinder causes deviation; A poor earth connection reduces light and starting speed. Both systems require correct method and components. Converting to 12 volts or discs may be practical, but must be documented and weighed against originality.

mantenimiento: In a 356, frequency matters: oil, lubrication of planned points, valves, ignition, carburettors and leaks must be checked at short intervals and also by time. Record the setting of each valve; a trend is worth more than a sheet that only says review done.

Clean meshes, check the fan motor belt and its shims, air ducts and compartment sealing. An air-cooled engine depends on plates, perimeter rubber and thermostat being present and mounted. Chrome parts or paint do not compensate for recirculated hot air.

Renew brake fluid on time, adjust drums when appropriate and check bearings, pivots, shock absorbers and steering. Lubricates hinges, closures and cables. In a 6 volt system, keep batteries, grounds and cable sections in their original working condition.

Use the car regularly and reach temperature without demanding it when cold. Before long periods, it protects fuel and battery and prevents humidity. An annual inspection of cavities and drains allows corrosion to be treated before it requires opening the body.
loQueHemosHecho: The restoration processes published by Valentín Motors show the criteria applicable to the 356: document disassembly, eliminate corrosion instead of covering it and check dimensions before closing and painting.
For a particular unit, the range should be decided after inspecting metal, numbers and mechanics. We don't automatically move the budget from another classic to a 356.
aQuienLeConviene: It is suitable for those who enjoy light and engaging driving at moderate speeds, accept frequent maintenance and value documentation and restoration quality over power. A 356 C usually makes it easier to use; an A, Speedster or Carrera adds rarity and more demanding research.

It is not suitable for those who need protection, air conditioning and braking in a modern car or want to leave it unattended for months. A 911 F offers more performance while retaining classic character; a 912 can give similar sensations at a different valuation; a replica must be purchased and insured for what it is.

guias.title: Porsche 911 G guide: versions, common faults and buying advice
guias.metaTitulo: Porsche 911 G: buying guide, common faults and servicing
guias.metaDescripcion: Porsche 911 G guide, 1974 to 1989: 2.7, Carrera 3.0, SC and 3.2, rust, engine, CIS, 915 or G50 gearbox and pre-purchase checks.
guias.excerpt: Not all Porsche 911 G are inspected in the same way: critical points of the 2.7, Carrera 3.0, SC and Carrera 3.2 before deciding on a purchase.
entradilla: The G series maintained the silhouette of the 911 with bellows bumpers for sixteen years, but under that appearance 2.7, Carrera 3.0, SC 3.0 and Carrera 3.2 engines coexist, as well as different gearboxes, injection systems and trim. The commercial name is not enough to buy parts or to anticipate common faults; first establish the model year, market and configuration.

In the workshop, the most expensive problems usually come from three areas: corrosion or accidents repaired decades ago, an engine dismantled without documentation and deferred maintenance on fuel, ignition and gearbox. A restored car is not automatically better. It is important that dimensions, internal protections, torques and tolerances have been respected, and that there is evidence of the process.

This guide excludes the 930 Turbo, which has its own guide. Its objective is to help you separate the particularities of each naturally aspirated version and prepare a useful pre-purchase inspection: cold start, lift, engine measurements, gearbox test and full body inspection.

versiones.texto: From 1974 to 1977, with different powers per market and version. Magnesium crankcase, temperature, studs and emissions make it especially important to know specification and previous rebuilds.
The European version retains 210 CV and the mechanical injection related to the RS. Its scarcity requires verification of identity, engine, intake system, bodywork and period components.
From 1976 to 1977, 200 CV, aluminium crankcase and CIS injection. It's a rare transition between Carrera 2.7 and SC; it should not be confused with a modified SC.
From 1978 to 1983, 3.0 engine and CIS injection, with European power that evolved from 180 to 204 CV. Sturdy when properly adjusted, but sensitive to air inlets, studs and system maintenance.
From 1984 to 1989, Motronic injection and up to 231 CV in Europe. It uses a 915 gearbox at the beginning and G50 since 1987; monitor valve guides, fuel lines, DME and gearbox condition.
Speedster, Club Sport, 3.2 WTL and commemorative series have specific elements and productions. The premium is only justified after authenticating options and ruling out a subsequent recreation.

antesDeComprar: Contrast VIN, engine and gearbox number, paint plate, market and options with the announced configuration. Over such a long period, engines, interiors, wings and gearboxes have been exchanged. Differentiate a reversible improvement from a unit that has lost identity without documentation.

Check battery and front panel, suspension support, wheel arches, pillar bases, side skirts, heating pipes, floors, window frame, rear tray and torsion bar supports. Look for corrosion from both sides and signs of recent welding or sealant.

Cold start without first cleaning the engine. Watch for smoke, noise, pressure and leaks. Measure compression and leaks, examine spark plugs and confirm that the crankcase, heads, cylinders and studs correspond to the invoices if the engine was rebuilt.

In CIS it checks system and control pressure, intake sealing, starter injector and accumulator. An SC that only starts either cold or hot is not tuned. In Carrera 3.2 check the DME relay, sensors, flow meter and fuel lines.

Test the gearbox completely warm. On a 915, the pattern and effort are particular, but scratching or ejecting a gear is not normal. In G50 check hydraulic clutch and flywheel. Separate bushings and external adjustment from worn internal synchronizers.

Check brakes, tyres, shock absorbers, ball joints and bushings before judging performance. In Targa and Cabriolet check door fit, reinforcements, soft top, drains and leaks. A floppy or crooked body is not corrected with an alignment.

averias.titulo: Hidden corrosion and old accident damage
averias.texto: Bubbles around the window frames or sills are usually the visible part of a larger area. Removing rubber or protections at selected points and measuring diagonals allows you to budget honestly. Covering rust reduces value and can weaken suspension anchors.

Loss of compression, leaks and stripped studs require checking magnesium crankcase flatness and threads. In cars with thermal systems in certain markets, temperature history is key. A correct rebuild includes machining and justified improvements, not just joints.

Difficult starting, uneven mixture or backfiring can end up damaging the air intake chamber. A relief valve reduces consequences, but does not correct pressures, ignition or air intakes. First diagnose the cause of the kickback.

Clicking, leaking at the base of the cylinder or chain noise when starting deserve immediate inspection. Updated turnbuckles are a known improvement, but their presence does not demonstrate the condition of chains, ramps or studs. Ignoring noise can disrupt the engine's timing system and cause internal contact.

averias.titulo: Carrera 3.2: valve guides and fuel system
averias.texto: Oil consumption and smoke during overrun can indicate guidelines; Odor or humidity in upper lines requires immobilization. The engine may continue to run with an aged line, but a leak on a hot block makes preventive maintenance a safety issue.

Scraping in second gear, vague selection, noise or heavy clutch requires distinguishing linkage, bushings, cable or hydraulic, clutch and synchronizers. Forcing the lever accelerates wear. Repairing early usually preserves more reusable components.

mantenimiento: Check oil and filter at least once a year, check screens or plugs depending on version and record pressure and consumption. Check for leaks on exchangers and hoses towards the radiator. Warm up by driving with a low load, not at prolonged idling.

Complete maintenance service includes valves, spark plugs, ignition, belts, filters and fuel system testing. In CIS it measures pressures; in Motronic it checks sensors and mixture. Checking fuel lines for age is as important as mileage.

Renew brake fluid, inspect calipers, flexible tubes, discs, bearings and handbrake. Lubricates and adjusts pedals, controls and closures. Gearbox and differential have specific oil and must be checked for leaks and particles.

Maintain suspension as a whole and align after correcting clearances and heights. Protect cavities and drains, especially after a repair. If the car is used little, it takes care of the battery and fuel and performs complete tours regularly.
loQueHemosHecho: The Magazine includes rehabilitations of 2.2, 2.7 and 3.2 engines, restoration of the CIS system, painting of a 911 G and complete projects on Targa of this generation.
The documentation allows you to compare how the diagnosis changes between an early engine, an SC with CIS and a Carrera 3.2, without turning a solution into a universal recipe.
aQuienLeConviene: It is suitable for those who want an air-cooled 911 with spare parts and specialists available, and are willing to prioritise the mechanical generation over colour. The SC is a balanced starting point; 3.2 facilitates diagnosis; the earlier 2.7 and Carrera require more research and may offer more historical character.

It is not suitable for those who expect modern driving, effective air conditioning without refurbishment or the absence of rust due to living in a dry climate. A 964 adds ABS and power steering; a 911 F is lighter and older; a 996 offers everyday use for less money, with different mechanical risks.

guias.title: Porsche 991 guide: versions, common faults and buying advice
guias.metaTitulo: Porsche 991: buying guide, common faults and servicing
guias.metaDescripcion: Porsche 991 guide, 2011 to 2019: naturally aspirated 991.1, turbocharged 991.2, PDK, PADM, cooling and checks to make before buying.
guias.excerpt: How to choose between Porsche 991.1 and 991.2 and what to check in PDK, cooling, dynamic engine mounts, chassis, brakes and electronics.
entradilla: The Porsche 991 gained a longer wheelbase, used more aluminium and made PDK the most popular transmission, while retaining the 911's 2+2 layout. The first series has naturally aspirated Carrera engines of 3,4 and 3,8 litres; the 991.2 uses a 3,0 twin-turbo. This changes the character, response and inspection priorities, although both have substantially more complex electronics and chassis systems than a 997.

From a workshop perspective, a 991 is not evaluated by mileage or digital history alone. It is advisable to read faults, hours, over-rev events, PDK adaptations, brake wear and status of optional systems such as PASM, PDCC, PADM, front-axle lift or rear steering. The more equipment is fitted, the more important it is to test each function.

The inspection must also distinguish official service campaigns from common faults and modifications. A leak, reprogramming or track use does not condemn a unit if it is documented and maintenance has been adapted; hiding them does alter the valuation and traceability.

ficha.valor: Six-cylinder boxer, 3,4-4,0 l; Carrera 991.2 twin-turbo 3,0 l

versiones.texto: 3,4 litres and 350 CV; the Carrera S uses 3,8 litres and 400 CV. They are the last large-series naturally aspirated Carrera and require checking cooling, injection, coils and consumption without applying M97 diagnostics.
Since 2015, 3,0 twin-turbo engine with 370 CV in Carrera and 420 CV in Carrera S. Check pressure, actuators, charge-air system and modifications in addition to the common base.
430 CV in 991.1 and 450 CV in 991.2, with specific chassis and equipment depending on configuration. Confirm options and parts, because many Carrera incorporate GTS elements later.
All-wheel drive and wide body; the Targa brings back the arch and adds a complex roof mechanism. Test the complete cycle, drains, glass adjustment and absence of warnings.
3,8 litre twin-turbo, all-wheel drive and PDK, from 520 to 580 CV in regular versions. Active aerodynamics, brakes and cooling require diagnosis and corresponding consumables.

versiones.nombre: GT3, GT3 RS and GT2 RS
versiones.texto: 3,8 or 4,0 litre naturally aspirated engines in GT3/RS and 700 CV twin-turbo in GT2 RS. Check campaigns, installed engine, track use, over-rev events, centre-lock wheels and carbon parts.

antesDeComprar: Separate 991.1 and 991.2 by VIN and engine, and download factory equipment. Check PASM, PDCC, PADM, Rear Axle Steer, Sport Chrono, Exhaust, PCCB and Lift. Each option adds value only if it works and has verifiable maintenance.

Read complete diagnosis before deleting faults: hours, mileage recorded in control modules, manual over-rev events, combustion faults, fuel pressure, actuators, temperatures and PDK values. Compare hours with steering wheel, pedals, seat, discs and tyre wear.

Cold start, listen to chains and tappets, observe smoke and check pressure and temperature until stable. In 991.2 it records boost pressure and looks for whistling, unresponsiveness or actuator repairs. A reprogramming requires more conservative maintenance invoices and testing.

Remove necessary protections to check radiators, condensers, pumps, switching valves, hoses and residue. Sweet smell or repeated fans are not solved by recharging air conditioning. Test circuit pressure if there are traces.

In PDK test maneuvers, smooth exit, changes at low load, reductions and working temperature. On manual models it checks the clutch, selector and over-rev events ranges. Check PADM mounts, which can fail electrically even if the car appears to drive fine.

Measure paint and underbody, especially on GT, underbody or lift cars. Check rims, PCCB discs, centre-lock wheels, tyres and geometry. A curb hit can affect the tyre, arm, and steering without leaving a visible repair on the fender.

averias.texto: Smell of coolant, variable temperature, active fans or intermittent warnings require pressure testing and activation with diagnosis. A clogged vacuum valve, pump, or radiator can produce the same general symptom; Changing the most accessible piece without measuring delays the solution.

A dynamic engine-mount warning may originate in the mount, wiring or control module. The car can still be driven, but control of drivetrain movement and the Sport function change. Read the fault codes and check both sides before automatically replacing the pair.

Shaking when starting, knocking, noise when shutting off, or slow shifting may involve clutches, flywheel, support, software, or hydraulics. Wear and adaptation values help separate causes. Ignoring the symptom until emergency mode reduces alternatives.

averias.titulo: PASM, suspension arms and rear-wheel steering
averias.texto: Bounce, drift, warnings or irregular wear should not be corrected with alignment alone. Examine shock absorbers, arms, ball joints, height sensors and rear axle actuators. Correct geometry on parts with clearance is short-lived.

Loss of thrust, whistling, inconsistent pressure or mixture failure require leak testing, actuators, sensors and turbos. A loose clamp and a worn turbo do not justify the same repair. Continuing to load can raise temperature and damage catalytic converters.

Warped door panels, peeling headliner, humidity or multiple warnings after periods of idling are common due to age and use. Clean drains and test battery and load before replacing modules; Low voltage generates secondary failures that confuse the diagnosis.

mantenimiento: Even if the plan allows longer intervals, an annual check with oil and filter is sensible in short, urban or sports use. Record consumption and open the filter if there is suspicion. Respect approved oil and temperature before demanding load.

The complete maintenance service includes spark plugs, filters, belt, coils, cooling, brakes and underbody. On the 991.2, also inspect the charge-air system; In direct injection, investigate injector failures or deposits only when symptoms and measurements support it.

PDK, differential and all-wheel drive service should follow time, mileage and use. Renew brake fluid, check PCCB with appropriate measurement and apply centre-lock wheels procedure. For circuit it reduces intervals and records temperatures and torques.

Keep radiators and drains clean, test batteries and update software or campaigns via VIN. After suspension, rear steering or tyres, perform calibrations and geometry. An update of technical maintenance provides more than accessories on a basis without history.

Before prolonged immobilization, check tyre pressure, fuel and battery, but avoid leaving the brake working on wet discs. When you recover the car, inspect for leaks and brake condition before demanding the engine and PDK.
loQueHemosHecho: The essential inspections and brake work published in the Magazine reflect the useful approach for a 991: complete diagnosis, measurement of consumables and post-examination estimate.
When there is no published case of this generation, we do not attribute to the 991 works of another model. The links serve as an example of a process, not a substitute for a specific inspection.
aQuienLeConviene: It is suitable for those who want to travel, use the car frequently and maintain 911 driving sensations with much more stability and comfort. The 991.1 offers naturally aspirated Carrera engines; the 991.2 adds torque and efficiency; GT and Turbo need a budget for tyres, brakes and active options accordingly.

It is not suitable for those who want visible mechanics and little electronics. A 997 is more compact and simpler; a 992 offers a more modern interface and aids, but adds complexity. Choose for use and necessary equipment, not for accumulating options that you are not going to maintain.

guias.title: Porsche 992 guide: versions, inspection and buying advice
guias.metaTitulo: Porsche 992: buying guide, common faults and servicing
guias.metaDescripcion: Porsche 992 guide, from 2019: Carrera, GTS T-Hybrid, Turbo and GT, PDK, electronics, cooling and what to inspect on a used car.
guias.excerpt: What to check when buying a used Porsche 992: digital history, campaigns, PDK, active systems, cooling, brakes and equipment.
entradilla: The Porsche 992 retains the architecture of the 911 and expands its daily usability with a wide body, more assistance and a more extensive electronic network. The first phase offers Carrera twin-turbo, Turbo and naturally aspirated engines in GT3; update 992.2 introduces, among other variants, the T-Hybrid system in Carrera GTS. That is why the exact name and model year determine any inspection.

Being a recent generation, the purchase usually includes warranty, campaigns, software and digital records. This is not a substitute for checking for wear and damage. A car with few kilometres may have accumulated track wear, underbody damage, damaged ceramic brakes or long periods with a low battery. Diagnostic readings should be checked against the physical condition.

This guide focuses on used cars and avoids presenting as a common fault what does not yet have a sufficient pattern. Warnings must be diagnosed by VIN, version and code; Product updates are ongoing. Before buying, confirm open campaigns and the current specification of the specific car with an authorised dealer.

ficha.valor: Six-cylinder boxer, 3,0-4,0 l; turbo, naturally aspirated or T-Hybrid
From 385 CV; depends on version and model year

versiones.texto: 3,0 twin-turbo engine, 385 CV in Carrera and 450 CV in Carrera S at launch. Available with propulsion or all-wheel drive, Coupé and Cabriolet, and PDK or manual depending on version.
Update started in 2024, with engine, aerodynamics, instrument cluster and infotainment changes. The powers and combinations evolve by year; Always confirm factory details by VIN.

The 992.2 GTS combines a 3,6 six-cylinder with an electric turbocharger and a high-performance hybrid system, with 541 CV of system power at launch. Its diagnosis and safety require specific training.
All-wheel drive, characteristic arch and automated roof. The complete cycle, glass adjustment, drains, sensors and possible noises must be tested several times, without obstacles or low voltage.
All-wheel drive, PDK, active aerodynamics and enormous thermal load. Power and technology vary with the evolution of the 992; check specification, cooling, brakes and any modifications.

versiones.nombre: GT3, GT3 RS, S/T and Dakar
versiones.texto: Variants with very different uses, from circuit to limited series or high height. Authenticity, campaigns, centre-lock wheels, underbody, brakes, hours and configuration outweigh comparing power alone.

antesDeComprar: Get the list of options and model year from the VIN. Verify campaigns, updates and remaining warranty with documentation. Differentiate a software-resolved notice from a replaced part; ask for a repair order and not just verbal confirmation.

Perform complete diagnosis without erasing memory: present and historical faults, hours, operating counters, temperatures, misfires, pressure, PDK and chassis systems. On manual models, check over-rev events ranges; in GT it relates data to circuit usage.

Inspect front end, radiators, condensers, underbody aerodynamics, wheel arches and lift points. In cars with nose lift, check for leaks, symmetrical height and repeated cycle. Underbody scraping can affect actuators or ducts even if the exterior bumper is intact.

Try PDK from cold: selection, slow maneuver, exit, smooth shifting and response to warm-up. Any knock or warning requires adaptation and diagnostic values, not assuming software behaviour. On manual models, check clutch, selector and consistency of recorded use.

Check PASM, PDCC, rear steering, active aerodynamics, exhaust, cameras, climate control, PCM, connectivity, lock and Targa or Cabriolet. The battery should be tested under real load: a discharged unit can generate a cascade of codes and hide the original fault.

Measure discs, pads, tyres and rims. At PCCB look for impacts and use appropriate measurement; in central closure confirms tool, procedure and torques. A set of Turbo or GT consumables changes the initial cost even if the car is within tolerance.

averias.texto: Simultaneous messages after weeks of shutdown usually require testing battery, load and consumption before condemning units. Clearing codes without stabilizing voltage removes context. A degraded battery can alter roofs, parking brake, chassis and communication between modules.

Odor, residue, frequent fans or inconsistent temperature call for pressure testing and guided activation of pumps and valves. The front accumulates debris and can lose efficiency. In high load versions, a small anomaly quickly becomes relevant.

Shock when selecting, shaking when maneuvering or limp-home mode may come from software, adaptation, flywheel, clutches, hydraulics or support. The diagnosis must retain codes and conditions of appearance. Continuing to drive in limp-home mode can increase damage and temperature.

PASM, PDCC, rear steering, aerodynamics and elevator share sensors and communications. A fault can deactivate several functions without all of them being damaged. Checking power, network and calibration avoids replacing modules due to correlation.

averias.titulo: Targa or Cabriolet roof and drains
averias.texto: Asymmetric movement, noise, humidity or position warning forces you to stop the cycle and locate the adjustment, sensor, cable or drain. Forcing the mechanism can damage panels and actuators. Preventive cleaning reduces water ingress into modules.

The Carrera GTS 992.2 incorporates high voltage components and an electric turbocharger. A warning should not be treated like a conventional 12 volt system. Immobilization, diagnosis and repair require procedures and qualified personnel to avoid damage and risks.

mantenimiento: Follow the plan corresponding to the VIN and record jobs by date and mileage. For short trips or sport use, an annual oil, filter, brake, tyre, cooling and underbody inspection provides a baseline even if the official interval is longer.

The full service includes spark plugs, filters and version-specific checks. PDK, all-wheel drive and differentials have their own fluids and procedures. Do not extend an interval just because the car indicates few kilometres if time has passed or it has worked on the circuit.

Keep software updates and service campaigns documented, and support the battery with compatible equipment during storage. Clean radiators and drains, calibrate driver aids after wheel alignment and check cameras or sensors after bumper removal. Work on T-Hybrid systems requires the correct high-voltage training and safe isolation procedures.

Check tyres for age, specification and wear differences, especially in all-wheel drive. Measure PCCB or iron discs with correct method. In GT and Turbo it registers centre-lock wheels torques and reduces intervals depending on temperature and use.

Keep a diagnostic report before and after each major intervention. In a generation still current, this traceability helps distinguish a software update, a campaign and a mechanical repair, and avoids interpreting the following notice without context.
loQueHemosHecho: The essential elements inspection published by Valentín Motors represents the starting point: identifying wear and warnings before turning a routine inspection into indiscriminate replacement.
Being an evolving generation, any case must be associated with VIN, model year and campaign. We avoid extrapolating an isolated failure to all 992.
aQuienLeConviene: It is suitable for those who want a 911 for frequent use, travel and high performance with current aids, and agrees to maintain software, battery, active systems and consumables. Carrera usually covers more uses; Turbo and GT only justify their cost if they will be used and cared for as such.

It is not suitable for those looking for analogue simplicity or who plan to keep the car without battery support and long-term maintenance. A 991 offers a slightly less complex modern experience; a 997 reduces size and electronics; a 718 can provide more space and balance for a different budget.

guias.title: Porsche 944 guide: versions, belts and buying advice
guias.metaTitulo: Porsche 944: buying guide, belts and common faults
guias.metaDescripcion: Porsche 944 guide, 1982 to 1991: naturally aspirated and Turbo versions, belts, water pump, clutch, transaxle and rust-prone areas.
guias.excerpt: What to check before buying a Porsche 944: belt and water-pump history, clutch, fuel system, transaxle, bodywork and electrics.
entradilla: The Porsche 944 combines a front engine and a rear gearbox in a transaxle architecture that distributes weight well and offers a very different drive than the 911. The range evolved from the 2,5 naturally aspirated to the Turbo and the three-litre S2, with brakes, suspension, electronics and interiors that change by phase.

Its purchase price may seem affordable, but a unit with outdated belts, original clutch, steering leaks and modified wiring soon consumes the difference. In these cars, preventive maintenance is not a generic phrase: losing the valve timing can bend valves and transform a pending inspection into a cylinder head repair.

The inspection should begin with evidence of the belt, rollers and pump, continue with fuel and cooling and end at the rear axle, clutch and body. A well-tuned 944 is stable and precise; one with worn out rubber bushes, tyres or geometry may look clumsy without the design being the cause.

ficha.valor: Four-cylinder front, 2,5-3,0 l; naturally aspirated or turbo

versiones.texto: First series since 1982, normally 163 CV in Europe, with initial interior. The later phase adopts oval dashboard and mechanical changes; Identify year to order valve timing system and components.
2,5 engine with 16 valves and 190 CV, from 1987 to 1988. Add chain and chain guide between shafts that must be checked in addition to the main belt.
Naturally aspirated version from 1989 with 165 CV and short production. Shares many late-stage needs, but displacement and some specific parts need to be confirmed.
3,0 16-valve engine with 211 CV since 1989, available Coupé and Cabriolet. Torque, brakes and daily use make it attractive, with special attention to the valve timing system and cam chain.
Since 1985, 220 CV; Turbo S and late versions reach 250 CV. Check turbo, wastegate, hoses, cooling, clutch and pressure modifications or electronic control unit.
Turbo S, Celebration and aftermarket series can provide specific suspension, differential, colour or equipment. Confirm codes and invoices before paying a premium for parts added later.

antesDeComprar: Ask for an invoice showing the date and mileage when the timing belt, balance shaft belt, rollers, tensioners and water pump were serviced. A paint mark does not prove which parts were fitted or whether the tension is correct. Without reliable evidence, budget for this work before driving the car.

In 16-valve engines, remove the necessary cover to assess the chain, chain guides, tensioner and shaft teeth. A broken chain guide or chain out of tolerance can damage the cylinder head. Don't assume that changing the belt takes care of this assembly.

Cold start and check oil pressure, smoke, vibration and noise. A poorly set or tensioned balance shaft belt alters the driving sensations. Check oil in coolant and vice versa, leaks in cooler housing and thermal stability.

Inspect the engine-bay fuel lines, pulsation damper, pressure regulator and injectors, as well as the rear hoses. Fuel odour or dampness requires the car to be taken out of use. On Turbo models, also check boost pressure, intake sealing, the turbocharger, wastegate and documented modifications.

Test clutch under load and during manoeuvres, and listen to the torque tube and transaxle in acceleration and overrun. A deteriorated rubber core causes looseness and knocking. Separate bearings, constant-velocity joints, differential and linkage before budgeting.

Inspect the sills, lifting points, wheel arches, battery area, roof, drains and tailgate instrument cluster. The rear window can separate from its instrument cluster, causing water ingress or noise. Check the retractable headlights, electric windows, instrument cluster, fans and air conditioning.

averias.titulo: Timing belts, balance shafts and water pump
averias.texto: Whistling, belt knock, pump leak or lack of history justify stopping use. A broken valve timing system causes contact between pistons and valves. Tension should be checked with proper procedure and tool after the specified settling-in period, not just during assembly.

Noise from the top of the engine, plastic fragments or thin chain guides are reasons to open the cover and inspect. If the chain jumps or damages the camshaft teeth, repair costs rise quickly. Replacement should follow condition and specification, rather than noise alone.

Oil in the expansion tank, emulsion or external leak can come from the cooler housing, but also from the cylinder head or other source. Test pressure and clean the circuit after repairing. Circulating with mixed fluids deteriorates bearings, hoses and thermal capacity.

Knocks when opening or closing the throttle and play in the drivetrain often appear as the rubber centre deteriorates. Continuing to drive puts strain on the torque tube and transaxle. Access is labour-intensive, so inspect the seal, bearing, fork and the rest of the assembly while it is dismantled.

Wet steering hoses dirty bushings and alternator; Aged fuel lines can cause fire. Do not treat as normal odour or periodic refilling. Locate correct pressure, material and route and clean to verify that the repair remains dry.
